summary: ASTROCARE is a smart footwear concept designed to monitor astronauts’ foot health and lower-limb activity in space. It uses pressure sensors, an IMU (movement sensor), and a temperature sensor to collect information about foot pressure, movement, and temperature. A microcontroller processes the collected data, stores it, and sends it wirelessly to a display for monitoring. The system aims to support astronaut exercise research, foot-restraint studies, and lower-limb health monitoring in microgravity. Optional features include vibration feedback and electrical muscle stimulation (EMS), which require specialist supervision and safety testing. ASTROCARE is currently a concept proposal, not a certified medical device. It requires prototype development, calibration, and proper testing before real-world use. It is intended to support existing space-health measures, not replace them.
details: ASTROCARE is a smart wearable space healthcare footwear concept designed to monitor astronauts’ foot health and lower-limb activity in microgravity. It uses pressure sensors to measure foot-contact pressure, an IMU to track movement, and a temperature sensor to monitor the foot–insole interface. A microcontroller processes the collected data, stores it, and sends it wirelessly to a display for monitoring. The project aims to support astronaut exercise research, lower-limb loading studies, and foot-restraint interaction monitoring. Its creative approach is to integrate multiple sensing functions into a single wearable insole. Optional features such as vibration feedback and electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) may be explored separately under specialist supervision. The proposed system considers comfort, low power consumption, data reliability, and user safety. ASTROCARE is currently a concept proposal that requires prototype development, calibration, and testing before practical use.
